Why Choosing the Right SUP Pump is Essential in 2025
Getting the right pump for your SUP will blow you away… literally! Modern SUPs feature enhanced drop-stitch technology and higher-pressure requirements, making pump selection more critical than ever. An electric pump is one of the best accessories you can purchase for your stand up paddle board. Whether it is your first time on a SUP or you are a professional paddle boarder, you can’t beat the hands-free ease of an electric paddle board pump. We put the most popular electric pumps for paddle boards through thousands of uses to find out which are the Best iSUP Pumps of 2024.
Electric paddle board pumps save you the energy of hand-pumping and help you get on the water faster. Instead of inflating your paddle board by hand and then getting ready to hit the water, you can change clothes, apply sunscreen, fill water bottles, and more all while an electric pump inflates your iSUP.
Electric SUP Pumps are designed specifically for the challenges of inflating a paddle board. They have two stages: a high-flow/low-pressure stage to inflate the board from flat to about 1 PSI and then a low-flow/high-pressure stage that brings your paddle board to its final pressure. Each pump has an automatic cutoff that you can set to your desired pressure. Once the board reaches that pressure, the pump will automatically turn off to prevent over-pressurizing your board.
In the past, electric SUP pumps have required you to connect directly to your car’s battery or plug into a 12v socket (“cigarette lighter”) in your car. But now, many electric pumps with built-in lithium-ion batteries can inflate multiple paddle boards extremely quickly.
Choosing the best electric pump for your paddle board boils down to whether you are looking for speed, portability, ease of use, or a bit of all three. We tested several electric SUP pumps for speed, usability, portability, and other measures. Here is our list of the Best iSUP Pumps.

Outdoor Master Shark III Electric SUP Pump
Availability: US, Canada, Australia, UK, Europe
Read Full Review

The Shark III Electric SUP Pump is Outdoor Master’s new Flagship offering. It boasts incredibly fast inflation times and the portability of a built-in battery.
Save
Features and Usability:
The Shark III comes with all the bells and whistles you could hope for. The pump itself has, of course, automatic inflation and deflation capabilities and can bring your board up to 20 PSI. It has an onboard active cooling system and a large LCD Display screen. However, like the Cachalot 2S, the screen is difficult to read in bright daylight.
You can control the pump’s settings with the four buttons located on the top of the pump. The screen indicates battery life remaining with color indicators around the edge of the screen. The Shark III also has different settings for inflating SUPs, Kites/Wings, and Air Mattresses, as well as a memory function to recall your preferred settings.
The biggest downside of the Shark III is its size. At 6.5 pounds and with a voluminous shape, it’s hard to forget where you put the pump.
Inflation Speed:
The Shark III takes over the top spot for the fastest electric pump we’ve reviewed, inflating our test board to 15 PSI in an average of 5 minutes.
Battery and Other Accessories:
The internal 74Wh battery has enough juice to reliably inflate three paddle boards. When the battery gets low, you can plug the Shark III into a 12v power source to operate the pump, though it inflates at a much slower speed than with the battery. The USB-C port can also charge your phone and other devices.
Bottom Line: The Outdoor Master Shark 3 is an ultra-fast and versatile rechargeable electric pump.

The Seawolf’s key feature is its massive internal battery. With a 10,000mAh battery, it has more power onboard than some eBikes! The Seawolf’s battery has enough juice to inflate our 11’x32″ test board to 15 PSI seven times and still has a little power left over to deflate them at the end of the day.
The interface is clean and easy to use, with four buttons and an easy-to-read, information-packed screen. There is a power switch on the bottom of the pump to turn the Seawolf on and start the internal cooling fan.
The Seawolf is easy to operate. There is one button to change units from PSI to Bar, +/- buttons to adjust the target pressure (up to 20 PSI), and a power button to start and stop the pump.

Best Electric Pumps for Inflatable Paddle Boards
As new electric SUP pumps hit the market, I continually test and evaluate them to keep this guide up to date. The recommendations below reflect the latest and best-performing pumps for inflatable stand-up paddle boards.
Are you tired of manually pumping your paddle board up to 15 PSI? You’re not alone. Few things are more frustrating than working up a sweat before you’ve even launched your board.
I’ve tested a wide range of electric SUP pumps over the years. I’ve learned that not all of them are created equal and they can differ significantly in:
inflation speed
maximum pressure
noise level
portability
and overall value.
Not long ago, there were very few quality electric SUP pumps to choose from. Fortunately, as stand-up paddleboarding has become more popular, manufacturers have stepped up their game.
Today, there are excellent options available for every budget, making it easier than ever to spend less time inflating your board and more time enjoying the water.
I have done extensive research on these pumps and used them myself many times over.
They not only work great for the majority of inflatable paddle boards but they can also be used for inflating inflatable kayaks, inflatable boats, inflatable mattresses, inflatable tents, inflatable pools and other inflatable gear.
Each of these pumps have pros and cons and fall into different price range categories so you can choose one that fits your needs and your budget best.

Most Common Types Of Electric Pumps For Paddle Boards
The most common types of electric pumps used with inflatable SUP’s are:
12V pumps that connect directly to your car battery with alligator clips
12V pumps that connect to an external battery pack
12V pumps that have an integrated rechargeable battery
pumps that connect to the 12V connection in your vehicle
air compressors (not recommended)
I’ll save you some time right from the start—an air compressor is one of the worst options for inflating a paddle board.
Without the proper adapter, it won’t even connect securely to your board’s valve. But even if you have the correct adapter, most air compressors are extremely slow at inflating an inflatable SUP to its recommended pressure.
I’ve tested this approach multiple times, hoping for better results, but it has consistently been disappointing. In my experience, it’s simply not worth the hassle.
Instead, choose a pump that’s specifically designed for high-pressure inflatable paddle boards and boats. These pumps are faster, more reliable, and capable of easily inflating your board to the recommended PSI. The models below are the ones I recommend.
1. OUTDOORMASTER SHARK II 12V ELECTRIC PUMP
I’ve been using the Shark II electric pump for several years, and it has never let me down. While newer models with extra features have come and gone, the Shark II has remained my go-to pump thanks to its consistent performance and reliability.
Outdoormaster has done an excellent job with the Shark II, combining impressive power with a practical, user-friendly design. Better yet, it’s priced in the sweet spot—offering premium performance without the premium price tag.
Where To Find The Best Deal
For the best deal and free shipping to the US and Canada for the Shark II electric pump go to Outdoormaster.com.
IMPORTANT FEATURES
This 12V electric pump has some great features as well.
5 Valve Attachments
The attachment you need for most inflatable SUP’s is the H3 valve attachment. I have used the Shark II with about a dozen different SUP brands and it has worked perfectly with all of them.
However it also comes with more attachments such as for a:
Boston valve
C7 valve
Pinch valve
805 Valve
With all of these attachments it also works great for inflating inflatable kayaks or canoes, dinghies, air mattresses and other inflatable products.
It also comes with four different sized gaskets (the white rubber rings) to ensure a tight seal when inflating your board.
Plugs Into 12V DC Car Connector
The Shark pump very easily plugs into the 12V accessory socket in your vehicle.
The power cord is 9′ long making it easy to reach the plug and the board.
Kink Free Hose
The 4′ kink-free hose is really easy to secure to the pump and doesn’t get kinked as some other flimsy hoses can.
Digital Display With Auto Shutoff
It has a digital display that is easy to read. There is no guessing at what PSI level you are at as you can see the progress on the display.
Once you set the PSI level it will automatically shut off when it reaches the set air pressure.
Lightweight
This pump is also one of the lightest options weighing only 3.6 lbs. and it is very easy to carry with the built-in carry handle.
It doesn’t come with a carry bag, which is unfortunate but I just keep mine in a canvas bag and keep it in my larger SUP gear mesh duffle bag.
Does Not Overheat
Most of the electric pumps for SUP’s on the market have a reputation for eventually overheating especially if you are inflating more than one board at a time.
This is not the case with the Shark II pump. It has a built in automatic cooling system that cools the pump down as it is working hard even when inflating multiple boards.

An electric pump is one of the best accessories you can purchase for your stand up paddle board. Whether it is your first time on a SUP or you are a professional paddle boarder, you can’t beat the hands-free ease of an electric paddle board pump. We put the most popular electric pumps for paddle boards through thousands of uses to find out which are the Best iSUP Pumps of 2024.
Electric paddle board pumps save you the energy of hand-pumping and help you get on the water faster. Instead of inflating your paddle board by hand and then getting ready to hit the water, you can change clothes, apply sunscreen, fill water bottles, and more all while an electric pump inflates your iSUP.
Electric SUP Pumps are designed specifically for the challenges of inflating a paddle board. They have two stages: a high-flow/low-pressure stage to inflate the board from flat to about 1 PSI and then a low-flow/high-pressure stage that brings your paddle board to its final pressure. Each pump has an automatic cutoff that you can set to your desired pressure. Once the board reaches that pressure, the pump will automatically turn off to prevent over-pressurizing your board.
In the past, electric SUP pumps have required you to connect directly to your car’s battery or plug into a 12v socket (“cigarette lighter”) in your car. But now, many electric pumps with built-in lithium-ion batteries can inflate multiple paddle boards extremely quickly.
Choosing the best electric pump for your paddle board boils down to whether you are looking for speed, portability, ease of use, or a bit of all three. We tested several electric SUP pumps for speed, usability, portability, and other measures. Here is our list of the Best iSUP Pumps.

Are you tired of manually pumping your paddle board up to 15 PSI? You’re not alone. Few things are more frustrating than working up a sweat before you’ve even launched your board.

portability

Not long ago, there were very few quality electric SUP pumps to choose from. Fortunately, as stand-up paddleboarding has become more popular, manufacturers have stepped up their game.
Today, there are excellent options available for every budget, making it easier than ever to spend less time inflating your board and more time enjoying the water.
I have done extensive research on these pumps and used them myself many times over.
They not only work great for the majority of inflatable paddle boards but they can also be used for inflating inflatable kayaks, inflatable boats, inflatable mattresses, inflatable tents, inflatable pools and other inflatable gear.

Without the proper adapter, it won’t even connect securely to your board’s valve. But even if you have the correct adapter, most air compressors are extremely slow at inflating an inflatable SUP to its recommended pressure.
I’ve tested this approach multiple times, hoping for better results, but it has consistently been disappointing. In my experience, it’s simply not worth the hassle.
